test_title: PYST 83: SSC GD Constable - English (Held On - 05 Mar, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: english
question:
Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully. Select the option 'no correction required' if the sentence is correct as given.

She was even more dreadfully fond of Estella (than she had been when) I last saw them together.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence as given is already correct and **does not require any changes.**
 
• The phrase **"than she had been when"** is grammatically correct and appropriately conveys the intended meaning.
 
• None of the other options provide a grammatically correct or meaningful alternative.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"She was even more dreadfully fond of Estella **than she had been when** I last saw them together."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: "then she have been when"** – This option is grammatically incorrect as "then" should be "than" and "have" should be "had".
 
• **Option 3: "than she has been when"** – This option is grammatically incorrect as "has been" does not fit the past perfect tense required here.
 
• **Option 4: "than she has been where"** – This option is grammatically incorrect and does not make sense contextually.
 
• **No correction required** – This is the** correct **option as the original sentence is grammatically correct.
